title: Scale House Standing Rule: Weighing, Probing and Applying a Load Under Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
Every truckload taken in under Grain Marketing Contracts is weighed in and probed before anything is decided about it.

**The member directs the load.** The member tells the scale house at the time of unload which contract the load is to be applied to, and that instruction is recorded on the scale ticket; where the member gives no instruction the load is taken into open storage in their name and applied to nothing. What the member says at the pit is taken as their direction, but it is the ticket that carries it, and the ticket number is what the load is afterwards known by.

**The contract must be live.** A load is applied to a contract only while that contract stands in active or delivering, so a load arriving against a contract still waiting to be countersigned is held on the ticket until the contract is countersigned. The standing is read off the contract record, and the load is correlated to it by the ticket number and the contract number together.

**Net bushels.** Net bushels are gross bushels less moisture shrink: bushels above the moisture base shrink by the shrink factor for each whole and part point above base, measured on the base for the commodity delivered, and grain at or under base shrinks by nothing and is never credited back. The moisture base printed in the catalogue is the yellow corn base; every other commodity uses the base carried in the table below.

| Commodity | Moisture base used at unload |
|---|---|
| Yellow corn | the moisture base printed in the programme catalogue |
| Soybeans | 13.0 percent |
| Hard red winter wheat | 13.5 percent |
| Oats | 14.0 percent |
| Grain sorghum | 14.0 percent |

Net bushels, not gross, are what comes off the contract's open bushels and what earns patronage.

**Delivery elsewhere.** Where the load is delivered to a facility other than the one the contract calls for, the freight differential is applied against the price, in the member's favour when the alternative facility is nearer the market and against them when it is further.

**Splits.** Loads may be split across contracts, and each split is written as its own ticket line so that the two parts never collapse into one another.

## Clause no longer in force

One clause of this rule is **no longer in force** and is carried here only so that no reader applies it:

> "A load carrying no price at all is routed into the member's unpriced position on the day it crosses the scale, and that date, not the date the paperwork is posted, is the date the carry clock starts from."
